module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# VCₙ dimension of convex sets in ℝⁿ, ℝⁿ⁺¹, ℝⁿ⁺²

In the literature it is known that every convex set in ℝ² has VC dimension at most 3,
and there exists a convex set in ℝ³ with infinite VC dimension (even more strongly,
which shatters an infinite set).

This file states that every convex set in ℝⁿ has finite VCₙ dimension, constructs a convex set in
ℝⁿ⁺² with infinite VCₙ dimension (even more strongly, which n-shatters an infinite set),
and conjectures that every convex set in ℝⁿ⁺¹ has finite VCₙ dimension.
-/

@[expose] public section

open scoped EuclideanGeometry Pointwise

namespace VCDimConvex

/-  ### What's known in the literature -/

/-- Every convex set in $\mathbb R^2$ has VC dimension at most 3. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 52]
lemma hasAddVCDimAtMost_three_of_convex_r2 {C : Set ℝ²} (hC : Convex ℝ C) : HasAddVCDimAtMost C 3 :=
  sorry

/-- There exists a set in $\mathbb R^3$ shattering an infinite set. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 52]
lemma exists_infinite_convex_r3_shatters :
    ∃ A C : Set ℝ³, A.Infinite ∧ Convex ℝ C ∧ Shatters {t +ᵥ C | t : ℝ³} A := sorry

/-  ### What's not in the literature -/

/-- There exists a set of infinite $\mathrm{VC}_n$ dimension in $\mathbb R^{n + 2}$. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 52]
lemma exists_convex_rn_add_two_vc_n_forall_not_hasAddVCNDimAtMost (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ C : Set (Fin (n + 2) → ℝ), Convex ℝ C ∧ ∀ d, ¬ HasAddVCNDimAtMost C n d := sorry

/-  ### Conjectures -/

/-- Not every convex set in $\mathbb R^3$ has
$\mathrm{VC}_2$ dimension at most 1. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 52,
  formal_proof using lean4 at
    "https://github.com/KitaKen1/vcdim-convex-counterexample/blob/ad7ffff1514843c886633f5408c6456dfb2e2a49/formal-conjectures-v4.27.0/VCDimConvexCounterexample.lean"]
lemma hasAddVCNDimAtMost_two_one_of_convex_r3 :
    ¬ ∀ {C : Set ℝ³} (hC : Convex ℝ C),
      HasAddVCNDimAtMost C 2 1 := sorry

/-- Every convex set in $\mathbb R^3$ has $\mathrm{VC}_2$ dimension at most 2. -/
@[category research open, AMS 5 52]
lemma hasAddVCNDimAtMost_two_two_of_convex_r3 {C : Set ℝ³} (hC : Convex ℝ C) :
    HasAddVCNDimAtMost C 2 2 := sorry

/-- For every $n \ge 1$ there exists some $d$ such that every convex set in $\mathbb R^{n + 1}$ has
$\mathrm{VC}_n$ dimension at most $d$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 5 52]
lemma exists_hasAddVCNDimAtMost_n_of_convex_rn_add_one (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
    ∃ d : ℕ, ∀ C : Set (Fin (n + 1) → ℝ), Convex ℝ C → HasAddVCNDimAtMost C n d := sorry

/-- Is it true that, for all $n$, every convex set in $\mathbb R^{n + 1}$ has
$\mathrm{VC}_n$ dimension at most 3? -/
@[category research open, AMS 5 52]
lemma hasAddVCNDimAtMost_n_two_of_convex_rn_add_one :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ ⦃n : ℕ⦄, n ≠ 0 → ∀ ⦃C : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n + 1)))⦄,
      Convex ℝ C → HasAddVCNDimAtMost C n 3 := by
  sorry

end VCDimConvex

reformulations.difference: Relative to the translates-only specialization of Naszódi–Taschuk Theorem 3, Lean allows arbitrary convex sets, rather than compact convex bodies with nonempty interior.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Any failure of a finite VC bound uses finitely many points and finitely many translating vectors. Take the convex hull P of all queried points required to belong to C. Then P is compact, lies inside C, and excludes every queried negative point. Thickening P by a sufficiently small closed ball yields a compact convex body with nonempty interior that preserves every membership test. Thus a counterexample among arbitrary convex sets would give a counterexample among convex bodies; the converse is immediate. No compactness or interior hypothesis is missing.

reformulations.difference: The declaration includes n = 0, whereas the standard VCₙ framework in On n-dependence uses positive n.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The additional case is true: hasAddVCNDimAtMost_zero identifies HasAddVCNDimAtMost C 0 d with C = ∅ ∨ C = Set.univ, independently of d. The convex singleton {0} in Fin 2 → ℝ is neither empty nor universal, so it witnesses the n = 0 existence claim. I proved both this case and the equivalence between the universally quantified existence statement over all naturals and its restriction to n ≥ 1 in /workspace/review/semantics.lean, without sorry.

Artem Chernikov, Daniel Palacín and Kota Takeuchi, On n-dependence, arXiv:1411.0120v2, Sections 2, 3.1 and 3.2. LaTeX source: https://arxiv.org/e-print/1411.0120v2

Artem Chernikov and Alex Mennen, Combinatorial properties of non-archimedean convex sets, arXiv:2109.04591v2, introduction and final remarks/questions, checked for related formulations. LaTeX source: https://arxiv.org/e-print/2109.04591v2

could_not_verify: VCDimConvex.exists_infinite_convex_r3_shatters: no reference is supplied for the stronger infinite-set shattering assertion. Naszódi–Taschuk Example 4 explicitly establishes arbitrarily large finite shattered sets, not this stronger formulation. Its paraboloid construction can be extended by indexing sections with all subsets of ℕ, but I could not verify the file's attribution of the stronger assertion to the literature.

VCDimConvex.exists_convex_rn_add_two_vc_n_forall_not_hasAddVCNDimAtMost: explicitly placed under 'What's not in the literature' and given no independent source. The semantics and boundary cases check out, and the higher-dimensional paraboloid construction supports the claim, but its exact source formulation and recorded research status could not be independently compared.
VCDimConvex.hasAddVCNDimAtMost_two_two_of_convex_r3: no independent source for this specific conjecture or its current open status was supplied or located.

VCDimConvex.exists_hasAddVCNDimAtMost_n_of_convex_rn_add_one: no independent source was supplied or located. In particular, I could not externally confirm that the intended conjecture requires a bound d uniform over all convex C, rather than a bound depending on C; the declaration does correctly match its own uniform-bound docstring.

VCDimConvex.hasAddVCNDimAtMost_n_two_of_convex_rn_add_one: no independent source for the proposed universal bound 3 or its current status was supplied or located. The answer slot, positive-n restriction, and mathematical definitions themselves were checked.
review.notes: No substantiated mathematical defect or contradictory status evidence was found. The cited counterexample proves exactly the file's negated VC₂ ≤ 1 statement. Its theorem bodies kernel-check unchanged; only an unqualified diagnostic #check needed qualification for this checkout. Both main proof declarations depend solely on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Successful scratch checks in boundaries.lean and semantics.lean cover empty/full sets, n = 0, n = 1, d = 0, the quantifier formulation of shattering, automatic injectivity of shattered grids, and invariance under additive equivalences. Infinite-set shattering is genuinely stronger than merely unbounded finite VC dimension and was not treated as an automatic equivalence. The paraboloid construction supports the stronger existence claims, but their precise external provenance remains unverified as detailed below.
